key_insight: Fast-ThinkAct compresses lengthy chain-of-thought reasoning into compact, verbalizable latent plans so agents can plan effectively with much lower inference latency while retaining decision quality.
problem_solved: Long, explicit chain-of-thought traces in vision-language-action tasks improve generalization but incur high inference latency, making real-time action in dynamic environments impractical.
method: Learn a latent planning space where multi-step reasoning is performed compactly, then decode short, human-interpretable verbalizations from those latents.
Train a two-stage pipeline: a latent planner that reasons in compressed space and an action actor conditioned on the latent (and its verbalization) to produce environment actions.
Optimize for a trade-off between plan compactness and fidelity (e.g., via distillation or joint training) so verbalizable latents match the performance of long CoT with much lower runtime cost.
impact: Enables fast, interpretable vision-language-action agents suitable for real-time robotics and interactive systems by dramatically reducing inference time without sacrificing reasoning quality.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: visual encoder -> latent planner (compact) -> verbalizer -> action actor, showing data flow and where latency is reduced.
Latency vs. performance chart: long CoT baseline (high latency) vs. Fast-ThinkAct (low latency, similar performance).
Illustrated example rollout: sequence of environment frames with compact verbalized plan and resulting actions at each step.
Table or icon panel comparing metrics: inference time, token length (reasoning trace), success rate across benchmarks.
paper_title: Fast-ThinkAct: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Reasoning via Verbalizable Latent Planning
paper_authors: Chi-Pin Huang, Yunze Man, Zhiding Yu, Min-Hung Chen, Jan Kautz
